headline: Highest risk is data leakage: RD-Agent’s broad API/network egress can expose sensitive research artifacts, while godot_rl_agents is local-only and adds little direct containment.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A has no network egress and no documented shared channel; B can run browsers and ingest external content, but the pair lacks a default bridge beyond manual transfer. Any injection would require unusual operator copying of B-produced content into A or vice versa, so the pathway exists but is limited.
conditions: IF the operator manually copies B-generated text into A’s prompt or files, injection becomes plausible.
IF a shared filesystem or clipboard bridge is added between the agents, the risk increases.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Avoid copy-pasting B outputs into A without review.
Disable browser-to-prompt ingestion in B where possible.
Use a provenance note when transferring text between agents.

B_data_leakage.rationale: A is local-only with no network egress, but B has broad egress, browser access, and handles logs, execution traces, and API keys. If the pair shares a workspace or A’s artifacts are fed into B, B can transmit those contents to third parties. The leakage path is plausible in default research workflows, though not proven by a shared filesystem field.
conditions: IF A’s outputs are placed into B’s logs or prompts, those contents can leave the local environment.
IF the operator stores secrets or sensitive reports in a workspace B can read, leakage becomes likely.
mitigations: Keep secrets out of any shared workspace.
Route B through a redacted input set.
Disable or minimize logging for sensitive runs.
Use separate directories for A and B.
Review outbound API destinations before enabling B.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A has no documented write or network surfaces, while B supports multiple instances and broad API use. There is no evidence of overlapping mutable resources such as a shared filesystem, git state, or shared OAuth scope, so direct write conflict is not established. Uncertainty stays low because the profiles do not show a common writable target.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same writable directory or repository, conflict risk rises.
IF B is configured to mutate shared files while A also writes there, collisions become possible.
mitigations: Assign distinct output directories.
Avoid concurrent writes to the same repo.
Use file locks for any shared artifact.
Run one agent at a time on mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: B is a research/automation agent that can act on outputs and use browsers/APIs, so if it consumes A’s generated artifacts as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream actions. A is a game-playing agent with no direct action authority, which limits blast radius, but the pair still supports an unverified handoff from A to B.
conditions: IF B treats A’s outputs as facts without verification, downstream research or API actions can be wrong.
IF A’s outputs are used as training labels or decision inputs for B, errors propagate.
mitigations: Require a human review step before B acts on A outputs.
Add a verification checklist for A-produced claims.
Keep A outputs labeled as untrusted.
Limit B to read-only analysis for A-derived artifacts.

E_compliance.rationale: A is open-source and local-only, while B processes financial reports, research papers, execution traces, logs, and API keys with broad egress. That creates a compliance mismatch if regulated or confidential data is routed through B, especially because B’s retention/logging surfaces are documented but not tightly constrained. A is not the compliance driver here, so it is not the cited risk source.
conditions: IF EU PII, PHI, or confidential financial data is processed by B, residency or retention obligations may be implicated.
IF B logs sensitive inputs to log/ or sends them to external APIs, compliance exposure increases.
mitigations: Exclude regulated data from B runs.
Redact logs before storage.
Confirm data-processing agreements for external APIs.
Keep sensitive artifacts in a separate, access-controlled location.
